correctness.rationale: With the forward incidence matrix E, Q_n=−EᵀE and A_n=−EEᵀ, so the heat intertwining holds including n=2. The norm at an edge is the variation of the corresponding Dirichlet kernel row with zero endpoints. Its discrete derivative evolves by Q_n starting at e_(i−1)−e_i. Each adjacent two-site Markov factor has nonnegative ordered minors (adjacency is essential); Cauchy–Binet and the Lie–Trotter limit give nonnegative ordered two-minors for the full heat matrix. Positivity then orders the two neighboring column ratios, so the row derivative changes sign at most once and the row variation is twice its peak. Strict Gram Cauchy–Schwarz at off-diagonal entries makes the global maximum a diagonal one. Odd reflection on the 2n-cycle gives K_t(i,i)=q_t(0)−q_t(2i); the consecutive radial differences satisfy the stated cooperative tridiagonal ODE with −3 end diagonals, including n=2. They are strictly positive, so exactly the central edges maximize, with the stated step attaining the norm. The sine expansion gives the finite formula and strict decrease. Killing removes paths that leave and return with positive probability, giving the strict lattice deficit, which vanishes along central sites at fixed time by the jump-count tail. For the scaled lattice profile put z=2t and r=I₁(z)/I₀(z); the logarithmic derivative in z is r−(1−1/(2z)). The Riccati equation gives slope −1/(4z²) at each zero; the function is positive near zero and negative at infinity by its leading asymptotic −1/(8z²). There is exactly one global maximum, and no finite path attains it. Independent root evaluation gave t*=0.3949892106717841 and constant 0.6630149334909871. Diffusive scaling follows from the fixed-mode sine and eigenvalue limits and the summable majorant exp(−4sk²).
residual_risks: Numerical root evaluation supports the decimals only. Conclusions use counting measure, rate one along each edge and unweighted adjacent differences; they do not transfer as stated to weighted paths or continuum derivatives.
